procedural_history.impugned_order: Order dated 04.11.2019 by the Trial Court summoning the appellants (accused) to face trial for offences under Sections 420, 465, 466, 467, 468, 471 read with 120B IPC.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The appellants filed an application before the High Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking quashing of the complaint and the summoning order dated 04.11.2019. The High Court dismissed the application and refused to quash the criminal proceedings and the summoning order.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellants, feeling aggrieved by the High Court's decision, appealed to the Supreme Court, seeking to overturn the High Court's judgment and quash the summoning order.

directions: The impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court dismissing the revision application is hereby quashed and set aside.

The order passed by the Trial Court dated 04.11.2019 summoning the appellants – accused to face the trial for the offences under Sections 420, 465, 466, 467, 468, 471 read with 120B IPC is hereby quashed and set aside.

issue.issue_text: Whether the allegations in the complaint and the evidence collected during the inquiry under Section 202 Cr.P.C. were sufficient to establish a prima facie case for the offences of cheating and forgery under Sections 420, 465, 466, 467, 468, and 471 of the IPC.

facts: A private complaint was filed against the appellants, alleging they committed cheating and forgery.

The complaint stemmed from the appellants' political party (SAD) filing an affidavit with the Election Commission of India (ECI) stating it adhered to secularism, as required by the Representation of People Act, 1951.
However, the party's constitution, in line with the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, restricts membership and participation along religious (Sikh) lines.
The complainant alleged that the party filed a false constitution with the ECI to fraudulently gain recognition as a political party.
The Trial Court and the High Court had allowed the case to proceed, issuing a summoning order against the appellants.
law: To establish the offence of cheating under Section 420 of the IPC, it is essential to prove that a person was deceived and fraudulently or dishonestly induced to deliver any property.
The specific offences of forgery under the IPC are defined as follows:
Section 466: Forgery of a record of a court or of a public register.
Section 467: Forgery of a valuable security, will, etc.
Section 468: Forgery for the purpose of cheating.
Section 471: Using a forged document as genuine.
application: The Court analyzed the allegations in the complaint to determine if the legal ingredients for the charged offences were met.

Regarding the cheating charge (Section 420), the Court found that the complaint failed to show how any person was deceived or dishonestly induced to deliver any property. It concluded that this essential element of cheating was completely absent from the allegations.

Regarding the forgery charges, the Court found that, on the face of it, the allegations did not fit the specific definitions. It noted that the case did not involve the forgery of a court record (Sec 466) or a valuable security/will (Sec 467).

Since the primary offences of cheating and specific types of forgery were not made out, the related charges of forgery for the purpose of cheating (Sec 468) and using a forged document (Sec 471) also failed.
The Court held that even if all the averments in the complaint were assumed to be true, they did not constitute the ingredients for any of the offences for which the appellants were summoned.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the allegations in the complaint and the evidence collected were insufficient to establish a prima facie case for the offences of cheating and forgery under the specified sections of the IPC. The Court found that the essential legal ingredients for these offences were not met. Consequently, it ruled that continuing the criminal proceedings would be an abuse of the process of law and quashed the complaint and the summoning order issued by the lower courts.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the allegations in the complaint and the evidence collected during the inquiry under Section 202 Cr.P.C. were sufficient to establish a prima facie case for the offences of cheating and forgery under Sections 420, 465, 466, 467, 468, and 471 of the IPC.
appellant_arguments: On the merits of the case, no prima facie case is made out for the offences for which the Trial Court summoned the appellants (Sections 420, 465, 466, 467, 468, 471 read with 120B IPC).
The complaint is an abuse of the process of law and the court, and therefore, the High Court should have quashed the criminal proceedings.
respondent_arguments: Considering the material on record and the evidence recorded during the inquiry under Section 202 Cr.P.C., the Trial Court was correct in being satisfied that a prima facie case was made out against the accused.
Neither the Trial Court erred in summoning the accused to face trial, nor did the High Court err in its decision.

statutes.act_name: The Representation of the People Act, 1951

ratio_decidendi.ratio: A criminal proceeding is liable to be quashed if the allegations, taken as a whole, primarily disclose a civil dispute and fail to establish the essential ingredients of a criminal offense, such as dishonest or fraudulent intent from the inception of the transaction.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: Looking to the averments and allegations in the complaint and even the material/evidence collected/ recorded during the course of the inquiry and even assuming the complaint’s averments to be true, the ingredients of the offence punishable under Sections 420, 465, 466, 467, 468, 471 are not at all made out.
legal_tests_applied: Whether the allegations in the complaint and the evidence collected, even when assumed to be true, make out the essential ingredients of the alleged offences.
policy_considerations: To continue the criminal proceedings against the appellants – accused arising out of the complaint and to face the trial by the accused as per the summoning order is nothing but an abuse of process of law and court.
